<!--
SHARED EXAMPLE TABLE for the dplyr lessons — pull it into a lesson with Quarto's include shortcode,
naming this file (see the "Before we start" section of find.qmd for a working example).

NOTE: do not write that shortcode literally in this file, not even inside a comment like this one. Quarto
resolves include shortcodes in a text pass that does not respect HTML comments, so a file naming itself
includes itself, and the render dies with "Maximum call stack size exceeded".

Five rows, two trips, using the real column names from the user's data so that what the learner practises
here transfers unchanged to their own records. Lessons that teach a dplyr verb should share this table
rather than declaring their own, so the same five rows carry across the course.

Two cells, and the split is deliberate:

 1. `library(dplyr)`, hidden with `include: false`. It has to run, but nothing in the audience can read
    `suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))`, and the alternative — a bare `library(dplyr)` — dumps
    a wall of "the following objects are masked from package:stats" at a learner who has been promised the
    page is simple. Loading a package is plumbing; keep it out of sight. The lessons still *name* dplyr in
    prose, which is what a learner needs in order to search for more later.

 2. the table itself, visible and editable, with one plain-English comment. This is the box the lesson
    talks about, so it must contain only what the lesson explains.

Anything written inside these fences is read by the learner. No authoring notes, no shortcodes, no jargon.
-->

::: {.lesson-plumbing}
```{webr}
#| include: false
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
```
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: true
# A small example table: five catches from two fishing trips.
example <- data.frame(
  trip_id      = c("trip_1", "trip_1", "trip_1", "trip_2", "trip_2"),
  landing_date = c("2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-05", "2024-01-06", "2024-01-06"),
  gaul_2_name  = c("Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Shimoni", "Vanga", "Vanga"),
  gear         = c("hand line", "hand line", "hand line", "gillnet", "gillnet"),
  catch_taxon  = c("Tilapia", "Snapper", "Octopus", "Tilapia", "Snapper"),
  catch_kg     = c(12, 5, 3, 8, 6)
)

example
```
